newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey reviving plan to upgrade aluminium smelter.
newsitem.headline: Turkey reviving plan to upgrade aluminium smelter.

text.p: Turkey is planning to dust off a plan to raise capacity at its only aluminium smelter as part of a government drive to exploit the mining sector, a government official said on Monday.

"We have almost completed the plan. We will submit it to (Prime Minister Necmettin) Erbakan either tomorrow or Wednesday," said Mustafa Aslan, press adviser to State Minister Teoman Riza Guneri, who is in charge of mining.
"We will amend related laws by the end of this year to get rid of legal obstacles and begin implementing the plans from 1997," he told Reuters.

The Seydisehir smelter plan, postponed in 1992 because of financial difficulties, envisages increasing the production capacity of the smelter to 100,000 tonnes from 60,000. It produced 61,514 tonnes of primary aluminium in 1995,
"The upgrade will cost about $255 million," said Aslan, but did not comment on how the government would finance the project.
"The project will be completed within 2.5 years," he said.
Production methods at the smelter, which has 248 pots, will be changed to what officials call a pre-baking system from the Soderberg system, adopted from the Russians.

Aslan said the plan included a legal change that would enable Etibank, the government company which fully owns the smelter, to operate a nearby power plant to reduce power costs to the levels accepted by other smelters in the world.
"Seydisehir spends 4.3 cents per kiloWatt-hour of power whereas the world level is 1.5 to two cents," he said.
He said natural gas to be supplied from Iran through a pipeline under an agreement signed last month would also help meet some of energy needs of the smelter, located in southern Turkey.

The plan was part of the government's drive to exploit unused ores and boost efficiency in current mines and processing plants, he said. The mining sector would help raise Turkey's export potential by about $5 billion from the year 2000.
The sector grew by 3.6 percent in the first half of this year after shrinking by 3.4 percent in the same 1995 period.
Mining exports were worth $405.6 million out of total exports of $21.6 billion in 1995.
He said details of the government's mining plans would be revealed later.
